key_insight: Training vision models with a human-inspired developmental visual diet shifts them to rely more on shape than texture, producing substantially more robust visual inference.
problem_solved: Reduces fragility of AI vision systems that over-rely on texture cues, providing a resource-efficient route to greater robustness against noise, perturbations and distribution shifts.
method: Design a developmental visual diet (a staged/curated sequence of visual experiences inspired by human infant visual development) for model training.
Train standard vision architectures on this curriculum and compare their feature reliance (shape vs texture) to conventionally trained models.
Evaluate robustness across perturbations and distribution shifts to quantify gains in shape bias and generalization.
impact: Practitioners can achieve more robust, shape-driven vision models without scaling compute or complex augmentations, enabling efficient deployment in real-world and low-resource settings.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing the developmental visual diet / curriculum stages used during training
Side-by-side bar chart comparing shape-vs-texture bias for standard vs developmental-diet trained models
Robustness curve (accuracy under increasing noise/perturbation) contrasting the two training regimes
Illustrative image triplets showing examples where texture-based models fail but shape-based (developmental-diet) models succeed
paper_title: Adopting a human developmental visual diet yields robust and shape-based AI vision
paper_authors: Zejin Lu, Sushrut Thorat, Radoslaw M. Cichy, Tim C. Kietzmann
